issues.body:
Acquire and assess the complete Sun et al. (2014) orthoclase weathering experiment

Primary lead: Sun De-Si, Yin Jian-Mei, Chen Ye and Cao Fei, “Effect of Crystal Structures of Potassium-Bearing Minerals on Aspergillus niger Growth Metabolism and Potassium and Silicon Release,” Scientia Agricultura Sinica 47(3):503–513, DOI https://doi.org/10.3864/j.issn.0578-1752.2014.03.010.

Round 71 acquired the official abstract and Chinese metadata page, but not the complete original:
- https://www.chinaagrisci.com/EN/Y2014/V47/I3/503 was readable through web search/open; urllib returned HTTP403.
- https://www.chinaagrisci.com/CN/10.3864/j.issn.0578-1752.2014.03.010 was acquired and exposed explicit PDF and RichHTML links.
- https://www.chinaagrisci.com/CN/article/downloadArticleFile.do?attachType=PDF&id=18009 timed out; web open also failed.
- https://www.chinaagrisci.com/article/2014/0578-1752/0578-1752-47-3-503.shtml returned HTTP403.

The abstract describes orthoclase containing minor muscovite and preferential muscovite weathering. Therefore its dissolved K/Si observations cannot yet be assigned to pure orthoclase. No new orthoclase owner or mechanism was created from the abstract. Existing potassium-feldspar-family evidence concerns a different, species-unresolved feed and is not a substitute.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Acquire the complete 11-page original through a legitimate changed route and retain acquisition URL, file type, nonzero size, checksum and page count outside Git. Inspect any original supplement or explicitly document its availability state.
2. Inspect specimen provenance, diffraction phase assignments, oxide/phase composition, all claim-bearing figures/tables, culture identification, leach conditions and controls.
3. Determine whether the evidence supports a species-scoped orthoclase record, a qualified mixed-specimen observation, an update to an existing broader owner, or continued deferral. Separate solution K/Si measurements from phase-specific mass balance and product recovery.
4. Check correction notices and the relation to Zhan et al. (2013), DOI10.4028/www.scientific.net/AMR.753-755.109, before treating them as independent replication.
5. If curated, save canonical history, named validation and independent native scientific review; preserve uncertainty rather than silently resolving impurity or crystallographic ambiguity.

Round 71 source assessment: research/sources/round71-silicates/20261014T122302Z-source-investigation.{md,json}. This is a source-acquisition follow-up, not a defect in the accepted nepheline record.
issues.title: Acquire and assess the complete orthoclase fungal-weathering experiment

issues.body:
Kato et al. (2022), DOI **10.3390/ijms23052483**, PMID **35269625**, reports lead-mineral formation with *Pseudomonas* sp. KKY-29. The complete original article XML, all 14 original figures, and the publisher's eight-page supplement were inspected for the proposed hydrocerussite record. They support a narrower mixed-phase observation but leave experimental mappings unresolved.

Evidence gaps:

- Results §2.6/Fig. 10 presents A–D in ascending phosphate order; the Fig. 11 caption gives the reverse order. The diffraction labels associate A with pyromorphite and D with hydrocerussite, while the discussion describes hydrocerussite at low phosphate and pyromorphite at high phosphate. A precise phosphate-to-phase assignment cannot be recovered consistently from these statements.
- Biomass dosing appears as mg/L, mg/mL and, in supplementary Fig. S1, g/mL. Supplementary Figs. S2/S3 support mg/L for their respective assays; this does not justify silently correcting all experimental descriptions.
- Diffraction was measured on processed, freeze-dried/crushed cell products. No matched sterile/killed-cell diffraction series or drying-phase control establishes biological necessity or the phase present before processing.

Follow-up:

1. Obtain a primary correction, author-deposited experiment map or raw metadata identifying A–D phosphate concentrations and the actual biomass concentration for each experiment.
2. Seek the complete synthetic-medium phosphate recipe, pH/shaking metadata and original diffraction files with preparation/control provenance.
3. Reassess the record only against verifiable primary material. Preserve the present mixed-phase, unit and condition limits if these gaps remain unresolved; do not infer a condition-specific yield, phase-specific intracellular location or industrial recovery.

This is an open source-evidence task, not a demonstrated defect in the deliberately qualified record. The round72 hydrocerussite dossier records inspected files and SHA256 values; existing lead and pyromorphite owners describe the same experiment, not independent replications. Initial all-state GitHub issue deduplication included all 147 non-PR issues and found no matching Kato/hydrocerussite task.
issues.title: Resolve Kato2022 hydrocerussite phosphate mapping and biomass units

issues.body:
The round72 orpiment record is deliberately limited to a source-assigned crystalline secondary phase in Liu et al. (2019), DOI **10.3390/met9121320**, already represented as the same experiment under arsenopyrite. It does not claim direct orpiment extraction or a phase-specific microbial increment.

Two verified primary publication leads could support a separate direct-substrate assessment:

- Shen et al. (2022), DOI **10.1016/j.chemosphere.2022.134287**.
- The Ag-assisted orpiment study (2015), DOI **10.1016/j.jhazmat.2014.09.022**.

Official Elsevier API responses supplied publication metadata, not the full original methods, figures or supplementary material. Abstract-only values have not been imported. Newman et al. (1997), DOI **10.1128/aem.63.5.2022-2028.1997**, cannot substitute: its inspected original explicitly describes amorphous As2S3, which does not establish crystalline orpiment.

Acceptance work:

1. Obtain legitimate full originals and relevant supplements for each direct-substrate study; record source URLs, access dates, nonempty hashes and access/license limits.
2. Verify phase-defined feed, impurities, organism/strain, acclimation and inoculum, medium, pH/Fe/Ag conditions, controls, time points, analytical methods and the denominator of any reported extraction.
3. Separate aqueous concentration from cumulative dissolution and isolated-product recovery; retain null or reversed effects and distinguish proposed pathways from measured results.
4. Update the existing orpiment owner only where justified, append canonical EDIT history, and save an independent exact-byte scientific review after validation. Otherwise document continued deferral.

The source investigation is retained at `research/sources/round72-arsenic-sulfides/20261014T131236Z.{md,json}`. This is an evidence-access task, not a corrective defect in the narrow existing observation. All-state issue deduplication included 147 non-PR issues and found no matching orpiment/realgar task.
issues.title: Acquire full direct-orpiment bioleaching studies and controls

issues.body:
The new `data/records/monohydrocalcite.yaml` intentionally preserves several unresolved primary-source discrepancies in Han et al. (2022), [DOI 10.1021/acsomega.2c02443](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.2c02443). These limits do not invalidate the narrow, explicitly qualified phase observations currently curated. Resolving them would permit a more reproducible and better-grounded mechanism description.

- **Culture versus sequence identity:** the paper identifies a cultured isolate as *Halomonas utahensis* WMS2 (Section 2.1 and SI Figure S1). [GenBank ON000249.1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/ON000249.1), checked 2026-10-14, instead records an uncultured *Halomonas* sp. clone WMS2, environmental sample, taxon 173971. The record uses genus 2745 only. Resolve the sequence-to-culture link and species assignment through an authoritative corrected accession, verified culture deposit, or published clarification; do not substitute the environmental-sample taxon as a cultured-strain ID.
- **Lowest magnesium arm:** Section 5.3 lists 0.01 M Mg with 0.01 M Ca, while Table 1/Figure 2 and SI Figure S6 label the lowest arm Mg/Ca 0. Obtain a corrected recipe or run mapping rather than assuming the methods value is a typo. Current MHC claims use explicit 0.07/0.09 M arms.
- **Ratio5/day140 phase assignment:** Section 2.3 assigns some morphologies to MHC, while Table 1/Figure 2 and SI Figure S6c3 assign aragonite plus hydromagnesite. Resolve the specimen/run labels with original diffraction/refinement files or a published correction. This disputed arm is not used as proof of MHC persistence.
- **Reproduction details:** Section 5.3 does not independently specify mineralization temperature/agitation or the 1% inoculum basis, and Section 5.4 omits harvest washing/drying conditions. The 37°C/120 rpm values occur in growth/salinity methods. Control photographs in SI Figure S4 extend only through 14 days. Clarification or original logs would permit stronger reproducibility and late-control assertions.

Evidence and exact acquisition hashes are in `research/sources/round72-carbonates/20261014T131835Z.{md,json}`. Complete primary JATS and original Figures 1–10 were checked, with the complete 19-page official SI. [Official SI DOI](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.2c02443.s001) provides stable access. The all-state 147-issue inventory queried 2026-10-14T13:13:24Z contained no match for this DOI, accession, WMS2 or monohydrocalcite; the exact local dedup receipt is `/private/tmp/cmm-round72-carbonates-issue-dedup.json`.

Acceptance requires an evidence-backed disposition for each discrepancy, exact source/run locators and preserved originals. Make only supported record changes, append canonical EDIT history when owner bytes change, run named validation and the required corpus/history checks, and save an independent native review of the resulting state. If primary clarification remains unavailable, retain the narrow qualified record and leave these source questions unresolved; new clean validation alone does not resolve them.
issues.title: Resolve WMS2 accession identity and Han2022 carbonate run ambiguities
